Name: Restaurant Papilio
Description En: This elegant restaurant done out all in white and with a beautiful high groin-vaulted ceiling is truly chic – you would never guess this space was once the château's stables. In the open kitchen, Jan Knedla and his team prepare a set menu comprising six, eight or 10 courses. Inspired by the chef's childhood, the dishes lean towards regional ingredients and are presented in a modern and creative style. Seats at the Chef's Table promise interesting glimpses of the action. Service is friendly and professional; the chefs mostly serve the dishes themselves and explain the idea behind them. They offer a very well-stocked wine list and the wines are presented charmingly and with profound knowledge. Also recommendable: national or international wine by the glass or the tea experience as a non-alcoholic option. In summer there is a nice terrace.

Name: Entrée
Description En: The Theatre Hotel not only wows overnight guests with its chic design, but it also offers an interesting dining experience based on an attractive modern concept. In the open kitchen, which can be seen from all over the restaurant, the team puts together modern dishes with light international accents. On the menu you can read for example "potato gnocchi, guanciale, whey" or "duck, chestnut, jerusalem artichoke, mandarin". There are three set menus, each building on the last with an increasing number of courses. The non-alcoholic beverage pairing is also recommended. In addition there is a good selection of cocktails.

Name: LEVITATE
Description En: Featuring an interesting combination of Nordic techniques, predominantly Czech ingredients and Asian spices from the owner's homeland, the cuisine here is rather unique. The resulting dishes are full of finesse and pleasing contrasts - served in 12 or 18 courses. The location itself is something special: unassuming from the outside, it has a surprisingly chic interior. Upon arrival, diners are first led to the bar in the cellar for aperitifs and nibbles – a distinctive blend of exposed old brickwork and modern design makes for an atmospheric setting. Once in the tastefully furnished main room, you have the choice to be seated at the long "private table" or one of the smaller round tables. You can also pay a flying visit to the chef in the "Living Room" and indulge in a few small dishes. Excellent service – the exceedingly friendly team is always on hand - everything runs smoothly and efficiently. Tip: The famous historical city park Riegrovy Sady and the National Museum are within easy walking distance.

Name: La Villa
Description En: A really lovely restaurant located slightly above the town… and it's not just the interior that is elegant and stylish – the food certainly holds its own. The classic/French-based dishes are subtly polished by the chef, as he brings in regional influences; this approach works particularly well with the saddle of fallow deer, for example. The best way to experience the handiwork of the kitchen is to opt for the set menu, "Le Pin". A vegetarian set menu is also available. At midday they only offer a simple lunch menu with two or three courses. Convenient: parking in front of the establishment.

Name: Štangl
Description En: A really interesting modern, open restaurant concept with a fully visible kitchen. They serve a three- or five-course menu based entirely on seasonal Czech ingredients. Without being fancy, the dishes are delicate and elegant, the flavours clear and well balanced. The atmosphere in the large, airy space on the first floor is pleasantly relaxed, and the charming staff are very professional and helpful. The sustainable philosophy followed here is explained in detail – a film projected onto the wall introduces you to the producers. Tip: The Eska bakery located on the ground floor sells house-made bread, as well as preserved vegetables and much more!

Name: Field
Description En: Two friends run this chic, minimalist restaurant in a stylishly understated way. Available in a longer or shorter form, their tasting menu comprises creative, well-balanced dishes with a strong focus on seasonal produce and Czech ingredients. Don't be surprised to see a sauce being flambéed tableside or smoke rising from a box (containing a delicious brioche glazed with duck fat)! The excellent medium-rare fallow deer also deserves a mention, as well as ‘Lamb, kale, watercress, green tea’. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team, which includes a sommelier, will be happy to recommend and explain apt wine pairings. The two different versions of the shorter lunchtime set menu are served on weekdays and at the weekend, respectively.

Name: ESSENS
Description En: The Classical building of the Chateau de Frontiere, which cuts a fine, stately figure, is named after the erstwhile Austria-Morovia border. High vaulted ceilings supported by columns and sleek design create a picture of elegance, in keeping with the stylish location. Large arched windows afford a view onto the property's gardens. The set menu showcases precise modern creations made with regional and seasonal ingredients – they even grow their own vegetables. Good examples of dishes are "grasscarp, bacon, thyme" or "lentil, nduja, celery". To accompany the food, they have excellent wines to recommend, often from great local winemakers, especially from the Morovia region.

Name: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise
Description En: This iconic restaurant is housed in an attractive historical building in central Prague. From one side of the L-shaped room, there is a prime view of the chefs at work in the completely open kitchen. Seasonality and Czech ingredients are the order of the day and elegant, modern and well-balanced dishes are served in a set menu format. The sleek interior has chic features, including a vaulted ceiling, striking chandeliers and a glass wine cabinet. Cheerful and relaxed service and atmosphere. The distinctive shape of the tiles in the kitchen is reprised on both the restaurant floor and the menu.

Name: Casa De Carli
Description En: Matteo De Carli and his wife Lenka Hermanová have been running their restaurant since 2012 after several stops around the world. The beautiful interior is straightforward and modern, with an open show kitchen and a walk-in wine fridge worth seeing as well as a wine fridge wall. Flavoursome cooking has a subtle North Italian bias, and the breads, pastas and ice creams are homemade. Make sure to consider the daily specials - the turbot in puff pastry crust, for exapmle, is a delight! Or let patron and chef Matteo surprise you with a 5-, 6- or 7-course tasting menu. In front of the house there are tables on the cobbled street. Tip: chef's table for max. 8 people in the basement - here the chef cooks right in front of you in a private setting.

Name: Valoria
Description En: The restaurant is a little way out of the city centre, but the journey south of Brno is worth it. They serve international cuisine with traditional, French, Mediterranean and Far Eastern influences. Chef Michal Černý and his team prepare both à la carte dishes and a seven-course tasting menu. Fresh ingredients go into flavoursome dishes such as "Spicy Thai soup, shrimp, oyster fungus" or "Mushroom risotto, Pecorino mousse, rocket salad" and "Confit of veal cheek, dill velouté, Carlsbad dumplings". When it comes to wine, the spotlight is on the Czech region of Moravia; the additional rum menu is also of interest. Friendly and attentive service is provided by a dedicated front-of-house team in the attractive contemporary interior. In summer diners are seated comfortably on the covered terrace. The adjoining room for special occasions is also pleasant.

Name: Šupina a Šupinka
Description En: The location here is truly amazing, within the grounds of Třeboň’s wonderfully restored castle, which you should definitely explore before or after your meal (there are shops, cafés etc). Or soak up the peace and quiet at the lake as you take in the view. The restaurant specialises in fish – try the carp chips (kapří hranolky) with mushroom and dill sauce, for which they are famous. Some of the fish on the menu come from the lake. The service is attentive and friendly. In winter you can sit in the elegant ‘Šupinka’, in summer the somewhat simpler ‘Šupina’ opposite is open - this is where the larger of the two terraces is located. Fish lovers will certainly get their fill here – but there is also lamb or game. They also offer apartmens to stay overnight.

Name: Long Story Short Eatery & Bakery
Description En: This on-trend, modern bistro concept – including a chef's table and open kitchen complete with Jopser grill – lies within the historical walls of a military bakery with lofty vaulted ceilings. The flavoursome cuisine is creative and seasonal, with an appealing à la carte menu, plus an extra dish at lunchtime. It's not easy to choose between dishes such as "Grilled oyster mushroom, cream cheese, bread chips", "Chickpea tofu, hoisin, yuzu, chard" and "Venison, rosehip, brussels sprout, semolina". Tip: The dishes also lend themselves to sharing, so you can try different things. Don't miss out on the terrific sourdough bread and sweet pastries. Café bar and hostel on the premises, too; public car park 100m away.

Name: MIURA
Description En: The interior design of this restaurant is sleek and modern, in keeping with the futuristic look of the hotel that houses it on its first floor. Diners sit in an airy, high-ceilinged room lit by chic designer pendant lamps – large floor-to-ceiling windows afford magnificent views of the surrounding countryside. Choose from an appealing selection of regional and international classics, or opt for the tasting menu. Full of flavour and depth, the dishes are testament to the skill of the kitchen team.

Name: Dvůr Perlová voda
Address: Kostelec nad Ohří 13, Budyně nad Ohří, 413 01, Czechia
Description En: This converted farmhouse has been given a modern facelift that has kept its charm intact. In a spacious, long room, tables are set out beneath a striking groin-vaulted ceiling; the kitchen, service counter and microbrewery have an open design. The copper brewery kettles are, of course, the most eye-catching feature, and it is definitely worth trying the beer. It is also interesting to see the chefs at work, as they cook up traditional, seasonal and regional dishes using top-notch ingredients. There is also a small "shop corner", which sells jams, preserves etc. Overnight guests can look forward to nicely kept guestrooms and a small wellness area. On a practical note, there are charging stations for electric vehicles.

Name: The Eatery
Description En: The 10min tram ride (line 6) from the city centre is definitely worth it! Contemporary Czech cuisine bursting with flavour and aroma goes at very wallet-friendly prices here. Done out in an industrial style, the place has a trendy and minimalist feel – the open kitchen fits perfectly into the picture. The service runs like clockwork, courtesy of a friendly and professional team. At lunchtime, the choice on the menu is smaller than in the evening.

Name: Na Kopci
Description En: As you enter, you leave the city outside the door. This highly appealing restaurant is located in a residential neighbourhood overlooking the surrounding area – fittingly, the name means "on the hill". Inside, the charming atmosphere is enhanced by a personal touch. The friendly service plays a part in this, as does the original wallpaper featuring pictures from the family photo album. The kitchen serves up a good selection of regional and classic dishes with punch, flavour and aroma. If you're having trouble deciding, start with the Chef's Starter Selection. And be sure to leave room for dessert – the "dumplings" are devilishly good.

Name: Šatlava
Description En: This attractive and immaculately kept restaurant is accessed via an inner courtyard. The bright winter garden is a particularly pleasant spot, and has a fireplace for cooler days. In spring and summer, the terrace on the balcony – with a view of the city park and spa gardens – is the place to be. The menu features seasonal and traditional dishes with contemporary, snazzy and on-point presentations. The experienced and friendly service is the icing on the cake.

Name: ATELIER bar & bistro
Description En: A cool location right in the centre. The Bistro, accommodated in a centuries-old building, is accessible via the impressive glass-roofed atrium courtyard, which boasts an inviting terrace. The tables laid out inside, where a relaxed atmosphere reigns, are also appealing. The space, done out in a trendy, pared-back decor, has a small bar and open kitchen, as well as eye-catching vaulted ceilings and art. The menu is small but enticing, and includes, for instance, steak or Italian influences. It is also possible to drop in just for a cocktail or glass of wine.

Name: U Matěje
Description En: Located in a pleasant residential neighbourhood not far from the zoo, this is an inviting restaurant in which an abundance of rustic wood finishings and decorative details such as numerous old photographs, striking pendant lamps and ceiling fans create a charming atmosphere. The food is a modern take on traditional Czech cuisine, eschewing unnecessary frills. Fresh, high-quality ingredients are prepared with precision to create delicious dishes such as carp fries with dill mayonnaise and coleslaw, stuffed goose stomachs and hearts with paprika and sour cream, or pulled goose meat with sauerkraut and potato pancakes. The reasonable prices are also something to smile about. In summer, the terrace with its mature trees is delightful! Friendly and attentive service. The restaurant STŮL in the same building operates under the same management.

Name: U Kalendů
Description En: This place is popular, and with good reason. The small menu is packed with regional classics – the hearty Czech dishes, including braised hare leg, pork cheeks and duck gizzards, as well as delicious desserts such as sweet yeast dumplings, are a real treat. And then there is the wonderful bread and fine pastries from the adjoining bakery! The select ingredients are not only beautifully prepared in terms of flavour and craftsmanship, but you also get a sense of the heart and soul that goes into the dishes. The decor is simple, with a slightly rustic feel. In the space at the front, the kitchen is visible through a window, and from your table in the area to the rear, you can see into the open bakery. The restaurant is just a few minutes from the centre, and only the street separates it from the Vltava River.

Name: Alma
Description En: This spot has all the makings of a favorite restaurant! The modern dining concept is reflected in the relaxed atmosphere and the trendy, urban interior complete with open kitchen and bar, as well as on the menu. The fantastic selection features mouthwatering options such as dry-aged beef and plenty of vegetarian dishes. The kitchen team works closely with local suppliers including KRO Bakery in Libeň, which provides excellent sourdough bread. In addition to a well-curated wine list, there is a wonderful range of cocktails – with or without alcohol. Delightful courtyard terrace.

Name: Štipec
Description En: It's no wonder this delightful restaurant in the city centre is a favorite among locals. The vibe is rustic and vibrant, the staff are exceptionally friendly and attentive, and the food is top-notch. Using select ingredients, the kitchen team delivers a contemporary take on Czech cuisine that is down-to-earth and packed with flavour. Signature items such as charred cabbage and short ribs are not to be missed. There is also a solid wine selection. In summer, the lovely covered terrace out front beckons.

Name: Bohém
Description En: Delicious and perfectly presented traditional Czech cuisine! With passion and culinary expertise, the kitchen team cooks up regional classics such as braised duck leg, rabbit and trout. A special mention goes to the Carlsbad dumplings – really delicious, fluffy bread dumplings! The moderately priced lunch special is very popular. The decor is chic and modern, and the service is friendly and professional. The restaurant is housed in the venerable Hotel Aplaus, very close to the market square, and boasts gorgeous guestrooms. Fun fact about the town: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the castle is the birthplace of composer Bedřich Smetana.

Name: Goldie
Description En: This restaurant housed in the long-standing hotel Nautilus, right in the historical city centre, exudes a sophisticated bistro atmosphere that blends the charm of bygone eras with a touch of glamour. In summer, the terrace giving onto Žižkov Square is a real draw. Go à la carte menu or opt for a four- or six-course tasting menu; a four-course vegetarian variant is also available. There is an additional, wallet-friendly lunch menu. The chef's specialities include "Sturgeon & Umami", traditional kulajda mushroom soup and fillet steak Rossini. Tip: Be sure to visit the city's labyrinth of alleys and passages (both above and below ground) and its historical buildings.

Name: Výčep
Description En: This pub-style place is loud and lively. Both the ambience and cuisine present as an unpretentious, modern interpretation of a traditional inn. Seated on a long bench at small wooden tables, diners tuck into this contemporary take on Czech cuisine and it is quite simply a delightful experience. Dishes such as potato dumplings filled with braised wild boar, red cabbage and bacon sauce are packed with flavour and full of soul – you can tell this is a team that knows what it is doing. The food pairs well with a glass of wine or a good beer.

Name: Dejvická 34 by Tomáš Černý
Description En: This somewhat labyrinthine restaurant has a pleasant, modern bistro atmosphere and serves both Czech and Italian cuisine. Quality ingredients and a lot of energy go into the flavourful dishes. The chef has a particular penchant for stews and pasta. Tip: One of the tables is located right in front of the kitchen and promises interesting glimpses of the team in action.

Name: Restaurant Perk
Description En: The restaurant is located in the modern Hotel Perk – the name of which is a reference to the town of Šumperk. The trendy urban interior is inviting. Make a beeline for one of the tables to the rear or, for a livelier experience, those directly opposite the open kitchen offer views of the chefs at work. The dishes are seasonal and are prepared with modern creativity and precision. Tip: Book an overnight stay in one of the hotel's comfortable modern guestrooms.

Name: Next Door by Imperial
Description En: Located directly opposite its parent establishment, Café Imperial, this restaurant boasts an elegant blend of modern and classical aesthetics. In a stylish and invitingly vibrant setting, a highly competent and well-organised team provides attentive service. To the rear of the dining space you can see the chefs crafting classic dishes in the open kitchen: braised beef with a creamy sauce and bread dumplings, or sautéed rabbit kidneys with mustard sauce – the extensive menu has something to offer every palate! Breakfast is also available, and the restaurant remains open continuously throughout the day.

Name: Dergi Praha
Description En: If you want to experience authentic Georgian cuisine, this restaurant in a commercial building just a few metres from the Vltava River is the place for you. Be sure to sample the classic khinkali, available with various fillings – they are second to none! The barbecued dishes, which are also packed with flavour, come accompanied by typical sauces. The setting is wonderfully spacious and cheerful: it features decorative elements such as traditional colourful pendant lamps and patterned fabrics. Live Georgian music adds to the atmosphere.

Name: STeaK Restaurant
Description En: Calling all steak lovers! The quality of the meat served here is fantastic, and the perfectly cooked premium steaks, as well as the sauces and side dishes are testament to the skill of the kitchen team. Tip: The cuts are rather large, which makes them ideal for sharing – consider booking for a small group. Adorned with rustic-looking decorative features, the decor is stylish and has an urban feel – the focal point is the open kitchen with its impressive barbecue. This place draws plenty of diners, who receive attentive service from the front-of-house team.

Name: Bockem
Description En: Good food and warm hospitality await in this 1905 townhouse located near the Vltava River and Kinský Garden. The enthusiasm of the team is palpable. The cosy, somewhat shabby-chic decor and the extremely dedicated, friendly and courteous front-of-house team make for a wonderful atmosphere. The food is cooked with respect for tradition, but also with a modern twist. In the morning, everything revolves around breakfast, but in the evening, the five-course set menu takes centre stage – think mouthwatering dishes such as beef cheeks with rose hip, cranberry and truffle, or the classic Bohemian sour soup.

Name: Benjamin
Description En: Ten seats are set around a horseshoe counter, chefs interact with guests, presenting carefully executed, boldly flavoured dishes, which are inspired by the Czech cuisine using only local products. The tasting experience starts at a fixed time in the evening, beginning with an introduction to the region's seasonal products staged in eight to ten courses. Wine pairings are offered to match.

Name: Sansho
Description En: The atmosphere here is trendy and lively with a friendly neighbourhood vibe. You'll enjoy an Asian-inspired cuisine, served by friendly staff – the "Beef smoked red curry: homemade sausage, pastrami & braised shin, spiced potatoes & fried shallots" is a tempting option, for example. Importance is placed on regional and seasonal ingredients, organic whenever possible. You can choose dishes à la carte or go for one of the set menus, which come in classic or vegetarian options. The affordable lunch set menu is particularly enticing.

Name: Pot au Feu
Description En: In his charming little restaurant, Jan Kracík serves food inspired by classic French cuisine and the culinary experiences he made during his years of travelling. Dishes such as veal sweetbreads with morels in sauce à la crème, or fillet of seabass with shallots and white wine sauce are available à la carte and as part of the "Menu Pot-au-Feu" or "Menu of the Season" (with options for each course). There are also a few daily specials. The welcoming atmosphere is enhanced by the friendly and laid-back, yet dedicated and knowledgeable front-of-house team, as well as a cosy modern decor with wine racks and art as decorative details.

Name: CottoCrudo
Description En: There are many reasons to visit this restaurant in the elegant Four Seasons Hotel: the charming location by the Vltava River, the chic ambience, the beautiful large bar and the terrace overlooking the river… And, of course, the Italian cuisine with a modern twist. Dishes such as vitello tonnato, house-made pasta, fresh sea bass or duck breast show off the exquisite quality of the ingredients.

Name: Yamato
Description En: This restaurant tucked away in the basement of a residential building is done out in a bright and minimalist modern style. As the name suggests, the cuisine is Japanese. In addition to classic hot dishes, there is a good selection of sushi and sashimi. To go with your food, there is sake and whisky from Japan.

Name: Aromi
Description En: This attractive restaurant is accommodated in a spruce historical house. The elegant modern interior, high ceilings and large, floor-to-ceiling windows make for a pleasing, airy feel. The open kitchen in the middle turns out contemporary Italian dishes – highlights include the fish and meat cooked on the oven grill. The excellent pasta is also a tempting option. Attentive and experienced service rounds off your dining experience.

Name: Grand Cru
Description En: Access to this elegant modern restaurant is via a cobbled courtyard. Inside, a warm colour scheme creates a pleasant atmosphere, and the front area features a light and airy winter garden. The classic cuisine with a Mediterranean touch is made with ingredients of the highest quality; example dishes include lobster soup or sea bass with white wine sauce. There are also different grilled dishes every day. Plus they have good wine recommendations up their sleeve.

Name: Na Spilce
Description En: This restaurant stands on the premises of the Pilsner Urquell brewery. Diners are seated in a lofty vaulted cellar featuring a modern-meets-rustic decor and a striking service station in the middle of the space. Modern Czech cuisine and traditional hearty beer-hall dishes are all meticulously prepared and packed with flavour. The chefs put a premium on regional ingredients sourced from local suppliers. Of course, a good beer goes well with it. Tip: For special occasions, you can book the ‘Schalender’ in the brewery's lager cellars. Also interesting: brewery museum and shop.

Name: LEAF
Description En: The restaurant is located in a residential area near the university. Behind the large windows, the decor is sleek and modern, with a raised bed of various types of cress and spices – which is integrated into the counter – providing a focal point. The food, mainly vegetarian, is served in the form of a four- or seven-course set menu. Ingredients are sourced from regional producers, with meat and fish used only sparingly. A wine flight has been devised to match the dishes. The service is friendly and professional.

Name: Malá Dvorana
Description En: In a side wing of the historical Grandhotel Pupp, this restaurant is accommodated in a magnificent hall. Elaborate mouldings on the ceiling and walls and an imposing crystal chandelier are a stylish throwback to bygone days; decorated with gold leaf, the modern glass bar in the middle of the room is also noteworthy. The contemporary dishes include pan-fried mackerel, sliced beetroot, leek mousse, honey, or chicken ballotine, Jerusalem artichoke, sautéed kale, chicken demi-glace.

Name: PRIME STEAK
Description En: The attractive modern interior of this restaurant tucked away in a building complex may come as a surprise – the small glass dry-aging refrigerator at the entrance and the kitchen, visible through a large window, draw the eye. As the name makes clear, steak is the mainstay of this joint, but there are other appealing mains, starters and desserts. Fish and seafood are available only if ordered when you book. At lunchtime, additional – and some simpler – dishes such as goulash soup or bratwurst make for a quick and inexpensive meal. The quality of the meat and the side dishes is on point! N.B. Parking can be tricky.

Name: Amano
Description En: This pleasant establishment that serves excellent cuisine is located on the edge of the old town. An interior with exposed brick and concrete walls, vintage-style furnishings and decorative wine racks creates a charming atmosphere. The open kitchen at the end of the dining area turns out modern Italian specialities. The dishes cooked on the open grill, which change every day, are highly recommended; be sure to try the pasta and risotto as well, and the all-year truffle specialities. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a four-, seven- or ten-course set menu. A fine selection of wines is also available.

Name: Divinis
Description En: In this really lovely spot, guests sit at tables laid out in several areas on different levels, surrounded by appealingly disparate furnishings. An abundance of individual details make for a charming backdrop – beautiful old floorboards, mismatched tables and chairs, original figurines, numerous books and designer lamps. Refined Italian dishes - prepared in the open kitchen - impress with their elegance and, above all, their flavour. The chef's signature dish is braised veal cheeks with Marsala, spinach and mashed potato with truffle butter. The friendly waitstaff are happy to advise you on the food and your choice of wine from the Italian-centric selection.

Name: Piano Nobile at Chateau Mcely
Description En: This wonderful castle estate, steeped in history and boasting superb grounds, now also accommodates not only a stylish spa hotel but also an appealing dining option. The elegant dining room boasts beautiful chandeliers, high ceilings and striking decorative porcelain displayed on shelves. When it comes to the classical French-style cuisine, choose between ambitious dishes à la carte or in the form of a tasting menu. They also serve a children's menu and event menus, eg Halloween or Christmas.

Name: Le Marché
Description En: This restaurant housed in a small hotel with a handsome Classical villa façade is a popular establishment. For starters, it enjoys an attractive location on the outskirts of the town, right on the banks of the Teplá – the riverside terrace is a romantic spot in summer. The seasonal cuisine is imbued with Mediterranean influences. In the evening, you can put together a three-course meal from a choice of several dishes or order the six-course tasting menu. At lunchtime, there is a somewhat simpler three-course set menu. Service comes courtesy of a well-staffed, very friendly and competent service team. Tip: While you are here, take a look at the spa centre with its colonnades.

Name: 420 Restaurant
Description En: Talk about an amazing location! Right outside the door, the centuries-old town hall with its famous astronomical clock dating back to 1410 captures everyone's attention – tables on the terrace are naturally coveted. Inside, the scene is no less arresting: This gorgeous building in the heart of the old town feels almost like a sacred space. With its soaring ceiling and period architecture, the restaurant is reminiscent of a church nave. Striking details such as a distinctive glass roof, phenomenal wall decor and sleek modern furnishings create compelling contrasts. In the open kitchen in the entrance, the chefs prepare contemporary dishes with classic foundations and influenced by regional traditions. Think pike-perch with semolina porridge, or Escoffier veal schnitzel with truffle sauce. Tip: The rustic vaulted stone cellar houses a shop selling house-made baked goods and meat products.

Name: Vallmo
Description En: An exceedingly inviting atmosphere awaits you in this restaurant tucked away in a small side street in Prague's New Town. The decor features light natural tones, modern furnishings and wall art. The kitchen team serves up seasonal Czech cuisine, combining traditional and contemporary influences. They also make a point of using locally sourced sustainable produce. In the evening, a tasting menu comprising five or eight courses is available. The sommelier recommends the perfect wine to accompany your meal - there is a beautifully curated selection. Shorter menu at lunchtime.

Name: QQ Asian Kitchen
Description En: A lively establishment, where it is fun to have a meal! This is partly down to the stylish atmosphere and the adept service from the pleasingly laid-back front-of-house team, but it is first and foremost thanks to the tasty and honest Asian cuisine, prepared for you by the Asian-born chef-owner duo. They will treat you to beautifully authentic street food and soul food dishes... the task of choosing is not an easy one. Sharing is also an option if you would like to try more of a variety. Tip: The cocktails are fantastic too!

Name: Monarch
Description En: The sort of steakhouse dreams are made of! The focus is, of course, on great cuts of meat – prepared to perfection. The USDA-certified dry-aged Black Angus rib eye is one nice variation on the theme, but there is also Czech steak. Onion rings are a worthy side, along with chimichurri sauce. Fish and seafood as well as pasta and risotto also feature on the menu. The whole experience is rounded off by the friendly, welcoming atmosphere and attentive service – the team is happy to advise you on your choice of steak. The wine list is also of interest.

Name: V Zátiši
Description En: This modern city centre restaurant is a popular spot. Its name means ‘timeless’ and with its clever blend of modern Czech and international dishes, it looks set to stand up to its name. In the open kitchen selected products are used. You can dine à la carte or in the form of a set menu, accompanied by the matching wine.

Name: Apelace21
Description En: The team here takes a highly professional approach, which is evident not least in the food. Dishes such as "St Jacob's mussels, blood orange, yuzu, crispy wafer, miso mayonnaise" and "lamb shoulder in diaphragm, Brussels sprouts, pumpkin croquette, almonds, pickled shallots" are prepared skilfully prepared with an emphasis on flavour. Easygoing yet highly competent and attentive, the service is also a highlight, including astute wine recommendations. Furthermore, the minimalist interior design, featuring decorative details such as a distinctive wine rack, artworks and modern pendant lamps makes for a truly gorgeous setting. Practical: The restaurant is located in a residential neighbourhood and is easy to reach by tram.

Name: Marie B
Description En: Set in a 14C townhouse, the restaurant is accessed through a covered courtyard entrance. Behind a somewhat shabby-looking front door covered in graffiti, a minimalist and trendy interior with an urban feel awaits. Beneath a rustic old vaulted ceiling, diners sit at a counter forming a U-shape around the open kitchen, they can watch the action up close. There are also two modern light installations by Berlin artist Anselm Reyle that draw your attention. Another interesting detail is the cookery book dating back to 1894, on display behind glass – it was written by chef Marie B Svobodová, after whom the restaurant is named. Comprising four courses, the carte blanche menu features creative modern dishes rooted in Czech culinary tradition. The nicely curated wine list places the emphasis on Moravian labels. The establishment also operates Vin de Marie wine bar in the same building.

Name: Taro
Description En: Since setting up shop in these new premises, brothers Giang Ta (maitre d') and Khanh Ta (chef) have been hosting diners in a trendy urban counter-restaurant. The chefs can be seen at work from the large U-shaped bar around the kitchen. A lively yet stylish atmosphere reigns, underscored by modern music. There is a seasonal five-course menu based on Vietnamese flavours and family recipes, influenced by the chef’s Vietnamese heritage and his life in the Czech Republic. The duck meat is dry-aged on site – you will notice it in the fridge behind the bar.

Name: Chapelle
Description En: With its chic design, clean lines, light wood and palette of natural hues, this restaurant is blessed with good looks. If you are lucky, you will be seated at a table with a front-row view of the chefs preparing the dishes in the open kitchen. The modern cuisine has international and Czech influences. Attentive and cordial service. Hotel U Kapličky located in the same building has attractive guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: ARRIGŌ
Description En: There's plenty to like here: The trendy concept not only covers lunch and dinner, but also breakfast, plus it has a café with pastries and delicatessen items. The space is modern and exudes a bistro flair; the open kitchen, in which seasonal dishes and smaller plates are rustled up, tends to draw the eye. The game dishes and the items cooked on the Josper grill, for example, are interesting options. Reasonably priced lunch.

Name: Babiččina zahrada
Description En: This restaurant in a quiet suburb of Prague has bags of charm. The interior is done out in a country-house style complete with lovingly chosen decorations. Outside, the terrace laid out in a gorgeous garden is inviting. The kitchen, which can be seen from the front section of the dining area, serves seasonal, regional and traditional dishes; a favourite is the beef broth with liver dumplings, vegetables and noodles, which is served in a pot to scoop yourself. And the steak tartare is prepared at your table. Friendly service. The hotel has cosy, attractive guestrooms, and the charging station for electric vehicles is a handy amenity. By the way, the name of the restaurant means "grandma's garden".

Name: Grandrestaurant Pupp
Description En: What could be better suited to this time-honoured setting than classic Czech cuisine? The lavish restaurant of the venerable Grand Hotel Pupp is housed in a magnificent space boasting high ceilings, an abundance of mouldings and stylish details such as fine chandeliers and mirrors, elegant fabrics and heavy curtains, all exuding a sense of history. An adept front-of-house team serves classically rooted cuisine with Czech and international influences. Both a set menu and à la carte options are available.

Name: Borgo Agnese
Description En: You'll feel as if you've been whisked away to the Mediterranean! The menu features tempting dishes such as "shrimp confit, potato, saffron aioli, radish", "gnocchi, mushrooms, pine nuts, beetroot, goat cheese, herbs" or "boar, cream, cranberries, semolina". Simply order à la carte, or opt for one of the tasting menus compiled from the same options. The delicious food can be accompanied by something from the extensive wine list, which features European labels, including some big names. Furthermore, diners enjoy attentive and adept service in a bright and classically elegant setting – a unique detail of the decor is the excavated historical church wall, protected by glass.

Name: V Bezovém Údolí
Description En: This handsome 17C half-timbered house in a picturesque village stands out for its unique architecture – it is one of the few remaining buildings of its kind in the Czech Republic. The attractive interior is minimalist in style and features a rustic wooden ceiling and a distinctive brick floor. Only regional, sustainably sourced ingredients are used in the kitchen, and the menu is intentionally concise. Dishes such as beef tartare with wild garlic mayonnaise, pickled shallot and herbs are refreshingly simple. Many components are produced in-house, including jus, oils, jams and compotes; the team also do their own fermenting and pickling. For overnight stays, there are five modern minimalist-style guestrooms and an apartment, all in a separate timber building.

Name: La Finestra in Cucina
Description En: Set in Prague's Old Town, this is a great establishment for top-notch Italian food. Made with select ingredients and clear craftsmanship, dishes such as calamari fritti, brasato al Barolo or spaghetti alla carbonara are sure to impress. Also of note is the fine selection of aged meats cooked on the grill. The tasteful decor teamed with red-brick vaulted ceilings is also inviting – and you can see into the kitchen through a window.

Name: Café Imperial
Description En: A truly magnificent setting! The restaurant of the Art Deco Imperial Hotel, a time-honoured establishment, occupies a stylish high-ceilinged room in which gorgeous historical ceramic detailing on the ceiling, walls and striking columns draws the eye. The atmosphere is lively without being hectic, and the service is well organised and professional. Featured on the classic-leaning menu is a good selection of dishes, including Czech favourites. As the place is worth seeing and attracts many guests, it's wise to book! Also open for breakfast, brunch, coffee and cake.

Name: Portfolio
Description En: Laid out over two floors of a charming historical townhouse, this restaurant is a popular spot that exudes modern chic. Clean lines, high-quality materials and warm hues create a tasteful setting. The inviting atmosphere is also enhanced by the friendly, attentive and well-trained service team. The internationally influenced menu whets the appetite with dishes such as duck breast, pumpkin with ginger, apple-rhubarb chutney and duck jus with red Kampot pepper, or dishes made from US prime beef. Good selection of wines.

Name: SAVOYA
Description En: The combination of a chic, modern vibe and modern regional cuisine with international influences is nothing if not inviting. The tasting menu gives you the best overview of the appealing range of dishes. The à la carte selection meanwhile has further options in store – and children are also catered for. The wine list includes well-known vineyards and names from the Old World, as well as a fine selection of champagnes. The restaurant is located in the Hotel Savoy, which is affiliated with the neighbouring Hotel Soyka.

Name: Kohout NA VÍNĚ
Address: Dům umění města Brna, Malinovského nám. 652/2, Brno, 60200, Czechia
Description En: This charming modern restaurant on the premises of the House of Arts is a cosy setting. The names of artists who, through donations, have contributed to the upkeep of the establishment are displayed on the ceiling. Wine plays an important role here, as the eye-catching floor-to-ceiling wine store suggests. As well as two tasting menus and a vegetarian set menu, there is an à la carte selection. The terrific wine list focuses on the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Hungary. They also use the Coravin wine system. Tip: Be sure to reserve, especially on weekends – they get fully booked quickly.

Name: Mlýnec
Description En: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location by the Vltava River in the heart of the city, right next to Charles Bridge. The chic and modern interior has floor-to-ceiling windows opening out onto a balcony terrace directly overlooking the bridge – you can also appreciate the view from some of the tables inside. In the open kitchen, the chefs create contemporary dishes, drawing on traditional Czech and international influences. Order à la carte, or opt for one of the set menus ("The Most Popular", "Tartare & Steak" or "Vegetarian"). There is also a lunch deal, and brunch is available on Sat and Sun. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and adept front-of-house team.

Name: Pavillon Steak House
Description En: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location in a small park near the centre. Sleek and chic design, high ceilings and large windows make for an airy atmosphere. As the name suggests, the focus here is on meat and different steaks. You choose the size and how you would like it cooked – the kitchen takes care of the rest. There is a variety of side dishes and sauces to accompany the meat.

Name: Parzival
Description En: After years at Prism in Berlin, Gal Ben Moshe is rising to a new challenge in Prague, bringing his Levantine-inspired cuisine to the elegant restaurant of boutique hotel Bookquet. A six-course set menu has been created under his direction – it is influenced by his Israeli homeland, but Asian influences can be detected, too. The wine pairings are also of interest. Almost all of the wines on the short menu are available by the glass. Enjoy an aperitif in the chic lounge in the hotel's lobby.

Name: Antricote Steakhouse
Description En: Just a short walk from the Vltava in Prague's Old Town, this is the place for steak lovers. The decor is trendy and urban with an industrial edge. In the open kitchen, the focal point is the wood-fired grill on which premium cuts of meat are cooked to perfection. These are accompanied by an array of side dishes and sauces. To kick off, there is also a tempting selection of appetisers. Tip for motorists: Old Town Parking is convenient.

Name: La Veranda
Description En: In this restaurant with the flair of an Italian country house and decorative shelves full of cookbooks, small tables make for a friendly, elegant ambience. The modern european cuisine is served à la carte or as a set menu. The front-of-house team provides attentive, competent service, and there is a good selection of wines to choose from.

Name: Sůl a Řepa
Description En: Once you have located the slightly hidden entrance, you find yourself in a world of fermentation, pickling and preserving – countless jars of various vegetables, mushrooms and the like are everywhere you look. The restaurant is pleasingly pared back, and some tables afford an interesting view over the pass into the kitchen. They source all ingredients from the region and, wherever possible, process these themselves. You can clearly see their sustainability concept in action here. The menu is seasonal, and the friendly waitstaff are happy to advise you as you choose.

Name: Cattaleya
Description En: This villa in a somewhat secluded location in the mountains is home to a small hotel with seven rooms, a spa and a terrific outdoor event area – and this elegant modern restaurant. In the beautiful light and airy glass pavilion with a round floor plan, ambitious contemporary dishes are served à la carte or as a seven-course set menu, with wine pairing on request.

Name: Tlustá Kachna
Description En: This inviting restaurant is located directly on the market square next to the small church. The two inviting dining rooms are done out in white with light wood furnishings and lovely cross-vaulted ceilings. There are also a few tables on the terrace in front of the building. The menu features flavoursome home-style regional fare such as braised rabbit leg with red cabbage and dumplings. Attentive service. The reasonably priced lunch deals are especially popular – reservations are recommended. In the evening, the cuisine is a little more upscale. Tip: Factor in enough time for a stroll through the pretty old town.

Name: STŮL
Description En: A little outside the city centre, surrounded by greenery, this restaurant is located right next to its sister establishment, U Matěje. There are just a handful of tables in the modern yet rustic dining space, all with a direct view of the open kitchen. Here, the young team of chefs creates an ambitious 5- or 10-course suprise menu. Attentive service comes courtesy of charming waitstaff. Tip for motorists: You can park in front of the building – using a parking app is recommended.

Name: U Štěpána
Description En: This small restaurant may be a little off the beaten track, but it's well worth coming here for the regional cuisine. Quality ingredients are skilfully prepared to impart plenty of flavour. The restaurant rears its own cattle, hence the focus on beef – delicious dishes include beef tongue with celeriac purée and horseradish foam, or beef ribs with coleslaw and bread. The interior has a charmingly rustic quality; in summer, dine out on the terrace, which is surrounded by greenery. Should you wish to soak up this rural idyll a little longer, there is also a campsite.

Name: Coda
Description En: Classic elegance is the name of the game here. The restaurant is located in the hall of the Aria Hotel Prague – herringbone floorboards, chandeliers and interesting objets d'art contribute to the stylish atmosphere. With its magnificent view over Prague, the roof terrace is a huge draw in summer! The restaurant serves refined Czech cuisine, a signature dish being their kulajda – a mushroom soup with a poached egg.

Name: Salabka
Description En: On the outskirts of the city, this restaurant is located in a vineyard with a wine-growing tradition dating back to the 13C. A combination of exposed old wooden beams, quarry stone walls and sleek modern furnishings creates an atmospheric setting. The view of the vines is best enjoyed from the tables at the windows on the first floor, which is actually a gallery constructed under the open gable roof. In summer, tables on the terrace are coveted. Meticulously prepared with great technical precision, the dishes are visually stunning and often feature produce from trusted farmers. Tip: Book a wine tasting or tour of the estate. For overnight stays there are six cosy, tastefully furnished apartments.

Name: ELEMENT
Description En: Lively and very much on trend, this restaurant enjoys a very central location in the city. Beyond the bar by the entrance (ideal for a cocktail), the dining space has an urban, industrial feel and features an open kitchen. The modern dishes created here – such as "grilled pork belly, ginger spinach, fermented black bean sauce" and "zander filet, confit leek, bean purée, parsley, Jerusalem artichoke" – are visually appealing and impress with their quality and bold flavours.

Name: Soyka
Description En: With its unpretentious feel, trendy modern-bistro style tweaked with a rustic touch, and pleasingly friendly service, this restaurant ticks all the boxes. And, last but not least, there is the regional, seasonal cuisine, in the form of a small but perfectly formed à la carte selection, including specialities from the Josper grill. Located in the hotel of the same name, this is the sister hotel of the Savoy right next door.
